title: Rav Achdevoi bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rav Sheshet’s student, as in [Bava Batra 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.9b.2-5): he answered him jestingly, and Rav Sheshet was distressed; Rav Achdevoi became mute. Rav Sheshet’s mother came and cried out before her son; he prayed for mercy and he was healed — so according to Rashi’s explanation. The commentator designated ר״נ explains that Rav Achdevoi bar Ami’s mother, who had been Rav Sheshet’s wet nurse, came so that he would pray for her son; and because of this they called him “Ulla who feels his way in his mother’s paths.”

Likewise in [Sanhedrin 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.55a.10-11) he asked Rav Sheshet, who said to him, “You have pained me.” And what they said there, “Rav Ashi said: What is your question?” Hyman considers a scribal error and proposes “his question.” In [Niddah 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.37b.9), Rav Achdevoi bar Ami speaks in Rav Sheshet’s name in one version.[^3] In [Chullin 113b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.113b.12), “he asked Rav,” Hyman proposes “Rav Sheshet,” according to Dikdukei Soferim.

Likewise he posed contradictions to Rav Chisda, as in [Pesachim 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.8), and challenges Rav Chisda’s words, [Chullin 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.70b.8). He is mentioned in [Shabbat 83b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.83b.3) (and Rav Yosef raises a difficulty against him), [Gittin 50a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.50a.15), Kiddushin 68b, [Bava Metzia 91a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.91a.11), [Zevachim 97a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.97a.3), [Chullin 114b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.114b.2), [Bekhorot 39a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.39a.15) and Me’ilah 13a.[^4] His mother is mentioned further in [Shabbat 109b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.109b.9), having made a remedy for someone. And what we find in [Temurah 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.30b.5), Rav Achdevoi bar Ami reporting in Rav’s name — this statement is cited in [Avodah Zarah 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.34b.13) with Rav Achdevoi citing Rav without the patronymic, and [Rashi explains](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.34b.13.2): the name of a sage. Had he been bar Ami, Rashi would not have needed to write this about a known Amora; Hyman instead proposes, according to Dikdukei Soferim, bar Avin or bar Mattenah. In [Bava Batra 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.9a.15-9b.1): “Rava said: Ulla, ‘who feels his way in his mother’s paths,’ told me in Rabbi Elazar’s name: What is the meaning of what is written, ‘And He put on righteousness as a coat of mail,’” etc.[^5]

notes.text: The supplied commentator siglum is ר״נ; the wet-nurse explanation matches saved Rabbeinu Gershom on Bava Batra9b, while Hyman’s supplied siglum remains disclosed. Ulla is part of the epithet attached to Achdevoi, not the person who bestowed it. Hyman’s epithet has מגשש, rendered feels his way; the saved Davidson and Rabbeinu Gershom witnesses have משגש, a distinct form, without a printed correction-history claim. Niddah has no locator supplied. Hyman’s name emendations and proposed identification with Ulla remain attributed, not a new identity merge.

The complete consulted Bava Batra 9a ending and 9b continuation place Ulla within the epithet, not as its bestower. Rabbeinu Gershom’s wet-nurse explanation remains distinct from Hyman’s printed commentator siglum; magashesh and the consulted meshagesh form are not silently equated. Niddah has no supplied locator. Hyman’s name emendations and Ulla equation remain arguments, not identity admission.

[Seder HaDorot 363](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=363&lang=en) supplies the location in [Niddah 37b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.37b.9) and cites [Chullin 113b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.113b.12), where the text reads Rav. On the latter, Heilprin proposes Rabbah or Rava, while Hyman proposes Rav Sheshet. The alternate wet-nurse interpretation appears in [Rabbeinu Gershom on Bava Batra 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Gershom_on_Bava_Batra.9b.12). Hyman’s text cites that interpretation under the initials ר״נ.

The linked Shabbat passage has Rav Achdevoi ask about the minimum size of an idol and Rav Yosef challenge the question. Gittin names Rav Achdevoi in the question about minors and adult heirs. In Bekhorot he asks about a missing internal organ.

Hyman cites Kiddushin 68b. The named objection in [Kiddushin 65b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.65b.3) concerns two men who arrive with a woman and a bundle. The text gives the full name Rav Achdevoi bar Ami.
